title: Mesa Reconstruction & Rebuild After Damage | Gold Water Fire | Phoenix, AZ
description: Reconstruction and rebuild in Mesa, AZ after fire or water damage. Gold Water Fire rebuilds drywall, cabinets, flooring and roofs. Call (480) 999-3339.
intro: The demo is done and now you are living in the part nobody warns you about. Studs where a kitchen wall used to be, a plastic sheet stapled over the hallway, fans gone, and a house that is dry and clean and still not yours. You have been keeping the file yourself since day one, calling the adjuster back, taking pictures, tracking who owes what. It is a lot to carry, and the rebuild is the longest stretch of it.

sections.heading: The rebuild depends a lot on when your street was built
sections.body: Mesa is not one housing stock, it is four or five stacked on top of each other, and that changes what putting a house back together actually involves. West Mesa and the older grid around Main Street and Country Club have postwar block and frame homes, some with lath-and-plaster walls, cast iron or galvanized supply lines, and original single-pane windows. When water or fire damage opens up a wall in one of those, matching the wall texture and the plaster profile is real work, and there is a good chance the framing bays are not on modern 16-inch centers. The Dobson Ranch and Fiesta District builds from the 1970s bring popcorn ceilings and older cabinet boxes that are no longer made in that size. Then east Mesa, out past Power and Signal Butte and into the Eastmark and Las Sendas areas, is mostly 1990s and newer production framing with engineered trusses, MDF baseboard, and slab-on-grade with post-tension cable, which matters a lot before anyone cuts or drills into a floor. A rebuild plan that ignores the era of the house creates repairs that look patched forever.

sections.heading: Monsoon and the long dry heat both leave rebuild work behind
sections.body: Mesa sits under the same summer storm pattern as the rest of the East Valley, and July through September is when the calls change. Microbursts push rain sideways into wall assemblies that never see moisture the rest of the year, blow gravel and debris off flat and low-slope roofs, and back up scuppers on the flat-roof sections common on older Mesa ranch homes. Water gets in at the roof-to-wall flashing, runs down inside the wall, and shows up as a stain on a ceiling twenty feet from where it entered. The other half of the year does its own damage: sustained heat cycles stucco and roof underlayment, dries out sealant at parapet caps, and hardens supply lines and water heater connections until a fitting lets go while nobody is home. Both patterns end the same way, with framing, insulation, drywall, cabinets and flooring that have to be rebuilt rather than dried.

sections.heading: One team from tear-out through the final coat of paint
sections.body: Gold Water Fire handles both sides of this. If mitigation is still in progress, the water or fire crew and the rebuild crew are the same company, which means the scope does not get re-argued at the handoff and nothing sits waiting for a second contractor to come look at it. Brandon Gurr is our Construction Manager and leads the reconstruction side, with Johnny as Reconstruction Team Lead running the work in the field. Kristine handles office and paperwork, and Brooke schedules water and mitigation work. We are licensed in Arizona under AZ ROC #264344, KB-2. A typical rebuild sequence runs framing and any structural repair first, then rough electrical and plumbing where lines were opened, insulation, drywall and texture match, paint, then cabinets, countertops, trim, doors and flooring last so finished surfaces are not the ones taking traffic. You can read more about the rebuild scope on our reconstruction and rebuild page, or start at water damage restoration or fire damage restoration if the cause is still active.

cards.heading: Texture and finish matching
cards.body: Knockdown, orange peel and older hand-troweled plaster all read differently in Arizona light. The goal is a patch that disappears, not one you can find from the couch.

cards.heading: Kitchens and baths
cards.body: Cabinet boxes, counters, tile and fixtures after a supply line or drain failure, including reworking a layout when the original cabinet run is no longer available.

cards.heading: Roof, stucco and exterior
cards.body: Decking, underlayment, flashing and stucco repair after storm or fire damage, tied back into the existing wall system so the next monsoon does not find the seam.

cards.heading: Insurance paperwork
cards.body: Scope documentation, photos and line-item detail written the way an adjuster reads it, so the rebuild estimate and the claim are talking about the same house.

sections.heading: What to ask any rebuild contractor in Mesa
sections.body: Ask for the license number and check it yourself at the AZ ROC website. Ask whether the rebuild scope is written line by line or as a lump sum, because a lump sum is very hard to reconcile against an insurance estimate later. Ask who is physically on site each day and who you call when something is wrong. Ask how change orders get approved, in writing, before work happens. Ask what happens to matching materials that are discontinued, since that is the single most common surprise in older Mesa homes. And ask for the sequence in writing, so you know whether flooring goes in before or after the cabinets and can hold the schedule to something. Good answers to these are cheap for an honest contractor to give.

faqs.q: Do I have to use the contractor my insurance company suggests?
faqs.a: No. In Arizona you choose who repairs your home. Your insurer can recommend a contractor and can set what it will pay based on its estimate, but the hiring decision is yours. What matters is that the contractor documents the scope clearly enough that the estimate and the actual repair line up.

faqs.q: Can you do the rebuild if another company did the drying?
faqs.a: Yes. We regularly pick up reconstruction after another firm handled mitigation. We will want to see the drying logs and moisture readings, and we will verify the structure is dry before we close any wall back up.

faqs.q: How much of the rebuild happens while we are living there?
faqs.a: It depends on which rooms are affected and whether kitchen or the only bathroom is out. Many Mesa rebuilds are done in phases with containment so the family stays in the house. We will tell you straight if we think that is not workable for your layout.

faqs.q: Which parts of Mesa do you cover?
faqs.a: All of it, from west Mesa near the Tempe line out through the Dobson Ranch and Fiesta areas to east Mesa, Red Mountain and Las Sendas, plus the surrounding Phoenix metro including Gilbert, Chandler, Apache Junction and Queen Creek.

cta.body: You have already done the hard part of getting this house through the emergency.
